title: Split Two Strings to Make Palindrome
summary: Given two strings of equal length, determine if splitting them at any index and concatenating the resulting prefixes and suffixes can form a palindrome.
statement: Given two strings of equal length, determine if splitting them at any index and concatenating the resulting prefixes and suffixes can form a palindrome. Each string can be split such that either the prefix or suffix can be empty. Return true if a palindrome can be formed, otherwise return false.
constraints: Choose one split index and combine a prefix from one string with the other string’s suffix. Either direction may form the palindrome.
hints: Match a prefix from one string against a suffix from the other from the outside inward.
At the first mismatch, only the unmatched middle from either contributing string remains undecided.
Perform the cross scan in both directions; accept if either remaining middle is palindromic.
All already crossed positions match, so the chosen concatenation is a palindrome exactly when one remaining middle is.
editorial: All already crossed positions match, so the chosen concatenation is a palindrome exactly when one remaining middle is.

tests.explanation: A one-character result is a palindrome for either boundary split.
Taking the prefix ula from the first string and suffix alu from the second produces ulaalu.
